summary: Contractor early exit: deprovisioning checklist + policy clarification for vendor-engaged infra access
description:
Issue summary:
A contractor (vendor: BlueRidge Analytics) on the Model Ops team has an early termination today (last day 2026-03-10). They have elevated access that was provisioned for a short-term onboarding project: Okta group membership, VPN access, AWS IAM role (redwood-contractors-mlops), GitHub org access (redwood-inference), and a dedicated set of SSH keys for a private Dedicated cluster. They are returning an M1 MacBook Pro and a company YubiKey they were issued.

Impact:
- Security risk if any credentials remain active (temporary dev keys in S3, active sessions to the Dedicated cluster).
- Billing/access risk if IAM roles remain and are used by vendor-managed automation.
- Compliance: vendor contract requires access revocation within 24 hours of termination.

Requested action (high level):
1) Immediately revoke Okta sessions and remove contractor from all Okta groups.
2) Revoke associated AWS IAM role sessions and rotate any shared service account keys that contractor touched.
3) Remove GitHub org membership and audit recent PRs/branches for secrets.
4) Disable VPN account and revoke any active certificates.
5) Revoke SSH keys on Dedicated cluster and schedule node credential rotation if keys were used for automation.
6) Coordinate device return and secure wipe with IT asset management (IMAC ticket).
7) Confirm YubiKey inventory and disable any 2FA keys linked to their account.
8) Provide guidance on whether we should immediately rotate the Dedicated cluster service account used by vendor pipelines (policy question below).

Current state / observations:
- Contractor confirmed they stopped all work and returned the laptop to the front desk at 14:35 local time; asset tag 2024-ML-129. IT confirmed receipt but has not completed wipe.
- Okta shows active sessions for the user in two browsers (last active 12:20).
- AWS CloudTrail shows STS AssumeRole events from the contractor principal within the last 4 hours.
- Dedicated cluster has two SSH fingerprints matching the contractor's key; cluster log shows kube access from that user yesterday.
- No clear list yet of which S3 objects or service accounts the contractor touched.

Policy question requiring decision from Security/People Ops:
- Do we perform immediate organization-wide rotation of the vendor integration service account used by the contractor (this will cause a temporary disruption to vendor-run pipelines), or do we perform targeted rotation only for keys we can verify were used? The contract stipulates 24-hour revocation of access, but rotation of shared service accounts is disruptive and requires vendor coordination.

Attachments / links (investigation starting points):
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0NTRACTS/p1642xx (internal-it + hr-ops)

workaround: Disabled user and revoked Okta sessions immediately to reduce active session risk. Blocked VPN account and removed GitHub org membership temporarily.
